sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. Newguineaworld, 'Ndeiram River' and 'Wanggom' pages (last modified 2024-06-25).
sources.note: Wanggom page is empty; Ndeiram page ('Sources', 'Historical phonology' under construction) names the only Wanggom source: 'Wanggom from Hughes (2009: 27-37)'.
No descriptive references at all; only subclassification refs (van den Heuvel & Fedden 2014; de Vries, Wester & van den Heuvel 2012). Alternative names Kombai, Wanggo, Wangom.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 2020. The Greater Awyu Languages of West Papua. Pacific Linguistics 664. Berlin/Boston: De Gruyter Mouton. pp. 4-5 and ch. 2.
sources.note: Ch. 2 sketches phonology only for Aghu, Digul Wambon, Kombai ('Kombai has contrastive stress in the form of a pitch accent on the prominent syllable', sec. 2.3.3) and Korowai; nothing on Wanggom. p.5: 'The morphological data on Wanggom are limited to a few paradigms written down in Baas' field notes (Baas 1981). We have no data whatsoever on Tayan.'

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue, 22nd ed., entry 'Wanggom' [wng] (Wayback copy).
sources.note: Nothing. 'Dialects: None known. Reportedly most similar to Kombai [tyn].' Population 1,180 (2002 SIL); Boven Digoel, upper Digul; classification Awyu-Dumut, Dumut; unwritten.

sources.citation: van den Heuvel, Wilco & Sebastian Fedden. 2014. Greater Awyu and Greater Ok: inheritance or contact? Oceanic Linguistics 53(1): 1-36.
sources.note: Wanggom is not mentioned (text search); Ndeiram represented by Kombai only. Family-level remark p.2 that in Greater Awyu 'lexical stress... seems to be distinctive' is not about Wanggom.

sources.citation: Wester, Ruth. 2014. A linguistic history of Awyu-Dumut. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
sources.note: Nothing for Wanggom; its Wanggom data are pronouns from Hughes 2009 (pp. 70-71). Historical phonology only.

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens, Ruth Wester & Wilco van den Heuvel. 2012. The Greater Awyu language family of West Papua. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, Special Issue 2012 Part I: 269-312 (Wanggom pp. 270-272).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. p.271: 'We have very little information on Wanggom morphology'; Wanggom data = Baas (1981) verb endings and Hughes (2009: 33) pronouns; p.272: 'The Wanggom wordlist of Hughes (2009) is in IPA. It is striking that all Wanggom words end either in a vowel or a vowel followed by a glottal stop.' Treats Tayan-Kombai-Wanggom as a probable dialect chain (de Vries 1993:1).

sources.citation: Hughes, Jock. 2009. Upper Digul Survey. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2009-003, 43 pp. Wanggom section pp. 9-10; Appendix V wordlists pp. 27-37 (Wanggom = Biwage II column).
sources.note: No statement: the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur in the report. The only Wanggom material is a c.220-item IPA wordlist from Biwage II with primary-stress marks (ˈ) as transcribed in the field, e.g. ˈhæmbʲɑ 'head', hɔˈlɔ 'eye', ˈhɔtɔ 'ear', ʔiˈdɔʔ 'finger', qutɑˈne 'woman'. My census of the marks (file above): disyllables penult 37 vs final 32; trisyllables initial 13 / penult 16 / final 17 -- i.e. no fixed position is visible in the transcription, but this is survey data, not a description.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 2001. Proto Awyu-Dumut phonology II. In Pawley et al. (eds), The boy from Bundaberg, PL 514. Footnote on Healey's grouping.
sources.note: Nothing on Wanggom stress; note only: 'Healey included a third language, Wanggom, in this group on the basis of a reference to it in Drabbe (1959:5). Recent research by de Vries has identified Wanggom as a dialect of Kombai (de Vries 1989:4).'

sources.citation: de Vries, Lourens. 1993. Forms and Functions in Kombai, an Awyu Language of Irian Jaya. Pacific Linguistics B-108. Canberra: ANU. p.1 sec.1.2; p.9 sec.2.1.3.1.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: open copy online: WID Offsite Storage Philol 69.57.3 no.108
sources.note: For Central Kombai only: 'Stress is phonemic' (p.9, minimal pairs foot/meat, red/penis). p.1: 'Kombai has three main dialects, Central-Kombai, described in this book, Wanggom and Tayan (see maps).' No Wanggom data.

sources.citation: Healey, Alan. 1970. Proto-Awyu-Dumut phonology. In Wurm & Laycock (eds), Pacific linguistic studies in honour of Arthur Capell, PL C-13.
sources.note: No Wanggom data: '(h) Wanggom is spoken to the west of Erimop and north of the Kaeti area' (location only).

sources.citation: de Vries, Peter Jan. 2012. Report on the Aerial Survey of the Upper Kao, Digul, and Eilanden Rivers in Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2012-025 (43 pp., 13.7 MB).

sources.citation: Versteeg, Henry. 1983. Zijn stam en taal. In Tj.S. de Vries (ed.), Een open plek in het oerwoud: evangelieverkondiging aan het volk van Irian Jaya, 21-25. Groningen: Vuurbaak.

sources.note: Five-page missionary note on the Wanggom people and language (lexical similarity 61% with Kombai, p.22); a stress remark is unlikely but it is the only Wanggom-specific prose that exists.

sources.citation: Baas, P.R. 1981. Unpublished Tsaukambo notebook (contains Wanggom paradigms). Cited in de Vries, Wester & van den Heuvel 2012:271 and de Vries 2020:5.
